sections.overview: Triakis maculata is a demersal houndshark of the eastern Pacific, from the Galápagos and Peru to northern Chile.
sections.identification: It has a robust body and rounded snout; small black spots are common, especially in juveniles, but may be absent in adults.
sections.habitat: It lives on the continental shelf, mostly inshore, at reported depths of about 10 to 200 metres.
sections.diet: It probably feeds on benthic invertebrates, but its diet is not well documented.
sections.behavior: It is caught by artisanal fisheries in Peru.
sections.reproduction: It is aplacental viviparous; sources report litters of about 14 young, with newborns about 30 to 40 centimetres long.
sections.ecology: It is a shelf-associated predator; the cited sources indicate limited biological knowledge, so its ecological role should not be specified further.
sections.conservation: The 2020 IUCN assessment, cited by the Peruvian IMARPE catalogue, classifies it as Critically Endangered.
